title.text: Scaling AI at Great Eastern: from proven use cases to measurable value

subtitle.text: Perspectives for discussion with the leadership team

title.text: Great Eastern already runs AI in advice, claims and compliance; the next gains depend on proving value and evidencing AI governance

head.text: AI is in use from advice to claims and compliance

body.text: Great Eastern has deployed an AI-enabled advisory platform for its financial advisers, rolled out a proprietary platform that automates medical claims, and uses AI to monitor transactions and sales for compliance risk.

head.text: Reported outcomes are speed and effort, not yet dollars

body.text: In 2025, 75% of medical claims were turned around the same day, and the advisory platform aims to cut adviser preparation time by about 75%; neither is reported with a baseline or a financial value.

head.text: Board oversight of AI exists; how AI itself is governed is not yet described

body.text: Two named directors are to receive fees for their work on data and AI initiatives, while the governance the report cites alongside AI is a service-quality scorecard and the Cyber Trust Mark.

callout.text: Three hypotheses to test together — page 6

title.text: AI is in use from advice to claims and compliance; complex-case underwriting is still in testing

title.text: Claims shows the clearest AI result; the adviser platform's benefit is still a target

label.text: of medical claims turned around the same day

detail.text: One of the fastest among Singapore’s health insurers, based on Ministry of Health service indicators

label.text: targeted cut in financial advisers’ preparation time

detail.text: The AI-enabled advisory platform “aims to reduce” preparation time; no achieved figure is reported

so_what.text: Neither figure is tied to a baseline or a dollar value — the evidence a board needs to fund the next wave of AI.

title.text: AI oversight reaches the board, but how AI itself is governed is not yet described publicly

items.text: Two named directors are to receive fees for their contributions to IT infrastructure, data and AI initiatives
The Board’s collective competencies include artificial intelligence and risk management
AI monitors transactions and sales patterns for compliance risks, including anti-money laundering and misconduct
The governance cited alongside AI is a Quality Assurance Scorecard and the Cyber Trust Mark
An inventory of AI systems and their risk materiality
Model risk management extended to AI

footnote.text: Annual reports rarely describe AI governance in detail; this reflects public disclosure, not an assessment of practice. Frameworks set at OCBC group level were not reviewed.

title.text: Three hypotheses would turn this outside-in view into decisions

col_heads: How the assessment would answer it

rows.text: Which three AI use cases would move Great Eastern’s claims and expense ratios most in 2027, and what are they worth?
rows.how: Size each candidate against Great Eastern’s own claims and expense lines, then rank by value and feasibility

rows.text: What would board-ready evidence of AI risk management look like, and how much can build on OCBC group frameworks?
rows.how: Map today’s AI systems to a risk-tiered inventory and show which controls group frameworks already cover

rows.text: What evidence would move complex-case underwriting AI into production, and what would it be worth?
rows.how: Define production criteria, test evidence and decision rights, and size the underwriting benefit

title.text: A 12-day assessment would test these hypotheses with your leadership team

columns.head: Value
columns.body: AI value pools sized from Great Eastern’s own numbers, with the three use cases worth funding first

columns.head: Governance
columns.body: An AI inventory and risk-tier view that a board and regulator can rely on, built to reuse group frameworks

columns.head: Scale
columns.body: Production criteria and decision rights for the next use cases, starting with complex-case underwriting
